rules.statement: Protection completes only when all three required layers have pairwise-distinct failure-domain identities.
Every layer representation verifies to the same qualified byte identity.
Operational SQL success alone never establishes backup or recovery readiness.
Recovery journal events are immutable and append-only.
Archive objects and manifests are content-addressed and never overwritten.
A restore candidate is never a verified restoration.
Restoration requires destination retrieval and exact verification for the closed object set.
Database dialect, placeholders, binary types, adapter, and connection protocol never enter object identity.
PostgreSQL is the first conforming adapter and cannot become the SQL portability contract.
Any missing layer, shared failure domain, mismatch, incomplete set, or unavailable source yields typed failure and no success.
Plaintext, unwrapped keys, private keys, and credentials are excluded from every layer and evidence record.
Protection and recovery claims are bounded to exact realizations, policies, failure domains, object sets, and observation intervals.
